1.
List has been revised.
Rejoinder affidavit filed today by the learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Shiv Mangal Pandey, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Mayank Maurya,
Advocate holding brief of Sri Mool Chandra Maurya, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Rajendra Prasad Singh, learned State Law Officer and also perused the material available on record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 132 of 2024, under Section 376 of I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 of POCSO Act, Police Station - Sidhpura, District - Kasganj, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: PROSECUTION
STORY:

4. The informant had instituted the FIR stating that his daughter aged about 14 years has been enticed away by the Gram Pradhan Omkar and was sexually assaulted by him thereby had impregnated her and subsequently got her foetus aborted.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT:
5. The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
He has nothing to do with the said offence as alleged in the FIR.
6. The victim is the consenting party as far as the applicant is concerned.

7. The victim in her statement has categorically stated that she had corporeal relationship with the applicant out of consent and was impregnated by him and her foetus was aborted by one Santoshi as she was pregnant by two months.
She has expressed her willingness to spend her life with co-accused person, who happens to be the maternal uncle of the Gram Pradhan.
8. The victim by her physical appearance seems to be major.
As per ossification test report, her age is stated to be 17 years.
9. Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.

10. The applicant is languishing in jail since 08.06.2024, having no criminal history to his credit,
deserves to be released on bail.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and shall cooperate with trial.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF INFORMANT/ STATE:
11. The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed and also the fact that the applicant has no criminal history.
CONCLUSION:
12. With respect to the age of the victim, a leverage of two years can be granted to the applicant on the upper side in light of the judgement of Supreme Court passed in Jaya Mala Vs. State of J & K,
(1982) 2 SCC 538 and Mohd. Imran Khan vs. State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi), (2011) 10 SCC 192,
whereby it has been opined that the radiologist cannot predict the correct date of birth rather there is a long margin of 1 to 2 years on either side.

sentences.text: 14. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been reiterated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
15.

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
16. Learned State Law Officer could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
17. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned State Law Officer.

18. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, pending trial and considering the complicity of accused, severity of punishment, at this stage, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

19. Let the applicant- Abhishek @ Aashu, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
Further, before issuing the release order, the sureties be verified.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement unfder Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
20. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.

21. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
